analyst_view.overall: Marseille (4th, 18 points) have won five league games in a row under Bruno Genesio, the last a 2-1 win at Lens before the international break, while promoted Le Mans (16th, 8 points) are winless in five and have conceded in every league game this season. Marseille miss only Emerson and Cornelius, both already counted, and are expected to line up much as at Lens: De Lange; Weah, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Ulisses Garcia; Nkada, Hojbjerg; Harit, Abdelli, Igor Paixão; Gouiri. Le Mans miss Bourabaa (their main creator, counted) and Sidibé; captain Samuel Yohou has recovered from the head knock he took against Monaco and is available, per Ouest-France, so their back three or five is near full strength. Referee Eric Wattellier (3.5 cards a game, lenient) is already in the numbers, and Marseille have a Europa League game on Thursday, though nothing points to rotation here.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals: Marseille's run of form adds a little, and Bourabaa's absence already takes a big share (about -19%) off Le Mans' goals. Yohou's return keeps the Le Mans defence as the numbers expect, and Marseille look set to name the same attack that scored at Lens, so nothing new moves me; I stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.0 corners, already trimmed for Le Mans winning few corners lately. Le Mans' 3-1-4-2 with wing-backs Buades and Calodat and Marseille's narrow attacking trio (Harit, Abdelli, Paixão cutting in) fit that picture, so I stay at 8.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and already take about 12% off for Eric Wattellier, who averages 3.5 cards a game. Le Mans have picked up more cards than expected lately, which is also counted; there is no rivalry or special stakes here, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots. Marseille have kept the same eleven for two games and are at near full strength, and Le Mans, with Yohou back, should be close to the side the numbers expect; with no rotation news either way, I stay at 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target, already slightly lower for Marseille's recent accuracy. Gouiri (7 league goals), Paixão and Harit are all expected to start and Le Mans have no clean sheet all season, but the numbers see that, so I stay at 9.4.
